chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a free woman whom her slave husband accuses (of adultery), and a free man whose slave wife accuses him. He said: 'They perform al-la'een (mutual accusation/oath-swearing).'

key_terms.يُلاَعِنُهَا: He performs la'een with her (swears oaths of accusation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of la'een when a free woman is married to a slave man or vice versa?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the judicial procedure of *al-la'een* (mutual imprecation) applies regardless of whether the husband is a slave or the wife is a slave, resolving potential doubts about social hierarchy affecting legal standing. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the core mechanism of oath-based divorce remains consistent across different marital configurations, ensuring legal certainty in cases of *zihar* or accusation of adultery.
